name: Zell Martin Busey
career: Lumber mill foreman (1930), crane operator (1940), National Guard caretaker (1950); a master sergeant by 1957.
sources: Ancestry.com, U.S. World War II Draft Cards Young Men, 1940–1947
Obituary of Gordon "Bud" Busey, Times-Standard, Eureka, California, 19 Oct 2005 (Legacy.com)
notes: Grandson of Aaron and Hattie Simons, living with them at Delta, Whatcom County, aged 4 in 1910. Inferred to be the son of Lola Simons and Matt Busey: Lola is the only Simons daughter known to have married a Busey. His name likely honours his uncle Raymond Zell Simons.
The 1910 census gives his birthplace as Washington, his father's as Iowa and his mother's as Michigan, which fits Lola Simons, born in Michigan.

Born 21 Nov 1906 at Bellingham, Washington (WWII draft card; other records give 1905 or 1908); died 28 Apr 1983 at Kirkland, Washington. In 1920, aged 14, he lived in Umatilla County, Oregon, as the nephew of Harry H. and Bertha Harrington, his mother Lola's sister.

Married Rose Lee about 1926 (they had twins Gordon "Bud" and Lola in 1929 and a younger daughter Ana Jean, and divorced in 1935); Jessie L. on 4 Mar 1939 in Seattle; and Grace M. on 31 Dec 1948 at Sedro-Woolley, Skagit County, with whom he had a daughter, Joan Cora, about 1949.
